set.body:
Shore up modules/design in the spirit of the hrf hardening pass. Full plan and measurements: docs/plans/design-hardening.md.

PREMISE, which differs from hrf. design is NOT stringly typed. Across 10,347 lines of main source there are zero Any, zero Map[String, Any], zero asInstanceOf, zero isInstanceOf, zero sys.error. It already has 14 opaque types, 32 enums, error ADTs with def message, and BaselineModel already parses closed sets into enums at the boundary — the pattern the rest of the module should follow. buildEither is genuinely total, and the formula already has a typed core: ModelFormula is a public, directly constructible AST that EventModelBuilder.buildEither accepts with no string involved.

The defect is subtler: in four places the types that exist are NOT LOAD-BEARING — constructed and then bypassed, duplicated, or discarded before they can do any work.

FINDINGS (all measured, all pinned by characterization suites):

1. A validated ColumnId can fail to name its own column. ColumnId.apply routes a lookup key through Names.sanitize, an OUTPUT formatter. ColumnId("my col").value == "my.col"; table.contains("my col") is true but table.columnById(ColumnId("my col")) is Left. The typed path fails exactly where the untyped one succeeds. Also not injective: "a.b" and "a b" collapse to one id.

2. Structured DesignError cases are discarded on the build path. 4 of 14 realistic user mistakes come back as BuildFailed(String), including "unknown column" despite MissingColumn existing for exactly it — DataTable.column throws, catchBuild catches and stringifies. MissingColumn is tested only by calling columnEither in isolation, never through the entry point.

3. Forty-four *Either twins. DataTable alone is 6 column types x 3 accessors = 18 methods, ~90 lines, for one concept. This is also the MECHANISM of finding 2: while a throwing accessor is in scope, a build path can pick it up by accident.

4. The formula AST is typed in shape but stringly in its references. ArgValue.Ident(value: String) carries a column name untyped from parse to runtime lookup — finding 2 is the symptom of this, not a separate defect.

5. Ten near-identical opaque id types, ~130 of DesignTypes.scala's 190 lines.

PHASES — a causal chain, not a priority list; each removes the precondition for the next. Both platforms green before the next starts.

  Phase 0  characterization (DONE — IdRoundTripProbeSuite, ErrorFidelityProbeSuite; design at 153 tests JVM+JS)
  Phase 1  make identifiers identify            bd-01KYYK1VED50YQP6FFSHX099HW
  Phase 2  one accessor per concept             bd-01KYYK2H2D2CTG506XJBA32J78
  Phase 3  type the AST refs, recover fidelity  bd-01KYYM0T0GX0AN6BZRY44VJWXG + bd-01KYYK1XFSXA49DQDRVDCT77KJ
  Phase 4  collapse the id boilerplate          bd-01KYYK2HF2MEJ9G3GV8B7FB90T
  Phase 5  optional col"..." interpolators (ergonomic only)

Phase 1 must be first: phase 3 types formula references as ColumnId/TermId, and doing that before the round-trip fix would push the silent-rename bug into the formula path, where TermId("a.b") rewrites a user's term name to a_b.

BLAST RADIUS (measured) — this is why the work is cheap:
  columnById and 5 siblings          1 consumer, and it is a test
  throwing DataTable accessors       3 main call sites, all in hrf/HrfGenerators.scala
  formula AST outside its package    1 downstream main file (fmri-workflow/AnalysisSpec.scala, 4 sites)
  string-literal formulas in non-test code   0
The .doubles(...) calls in motion and model are on unrelated fixture objects, not DataTable.

DECLINED, recorded at bd-01KYYM0W2VTVT4VBSYK9HYFXZG: no formula macro, no schema-typed DataTable.

ALSO NOT PROPOSED: re-typing the formula input (a formula is user text; String is the right input type for the parsing front-end); replacing basisClass/basis strings (they key a user-extensible registry, so an open set is right); touching BaselineModel's parsers (they are the good pattern); a design-laws module (hrf earned one because it has algebraic structure — design is compilation and bookkeeping, and laws here would be ceremony).
set.title: EPIC: harden modules/design toward load-bearing types
